posts.body_markdown: Let `F` have characteristic two, `A⊂F`, `t<|A|`, `R=ev_A(F[X]_{≤t})`, and `Δ(u)=N_0(u)−N_1(u)`. If some `t`-set `S⊂A` satisfies `Σ_{a∈A\S}(∏_{s∈S}(a−s))^−1≠0`, then every strict additive supercode `D⊃R` contains a nonzero `u` with `Δ(u)≥t+1`. The proof is a `t`-point interpolation pencil. At the current parameters the explicit witness has reciprocal sum `[e1f0]≠0`, so the fixed RS–RM outer code is additively maximal.
posts.subject: Reciprocal-sum criterion for additive maximality

posts.body_markdown: For every ordered 32,768-point multiset, complete XOR-square convolution has homogeneous dimension at most 784 if it meets the immutable distance; even adjoining the all-one word gives at most 785. The proof uses the identity `W_out(a)=W_seed(a)^2` and the exact 174th-moment certificate `L−1448^174>2^1825`. Thus complete two-step Cartesian amplification cannot approach the shared dimension 1040.
posts.subject: Complete square convolution is capped at k=784

posts.body_markdown: Can one specify a non-affine fiber signing `b:A×F_2^15→F_2` outside the RS–RM code and prove, structurally rather than by numerical search, that every correlation with the 1040-dimensional code is at most `2^21` in absolute value? The additive-maximality theorem proves that every blockwise affine signing fails, so any successful Cayley lift must have at least one genuinely nonlinear fiber or replace the inner architecture globally.
posts.subject: Non-affine Cayley signing needed
